rows.selection_reason: With no prior experiments, there is no evidence to exploit, so the goal is to establish a strong multimodal baseline that reduces uncertainty about whether the full pipeline (learned RNA encoder + strong image encoder + expressive aggregation) is viable. config_005 combines the most powerful image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), a learned RNA representation (scgpt), the most expressive aggregation (transformer), multiprofile (richer cellular information), and simple concat fusion (fewer hyperparameters to fail). This 'strongest expected' configuration serves as an informative anchor: if it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate individual components to identify what drives performance; if it underperforms, it signals that one or more of these choices (e.g., transformer aggregation or scgpt) may be suboptimal, redirecting the search. Under a 10-experiment budget, establishing this high-information baseline first is the best use of experiment 1.

With only one data point (config_005: multimodal/multiprofile/scgpt/imagenet_vit_l/transformer/concat at 0.507 acc), the most fundamental uncertainty is whether the multimodal architecture is actually necessary or whether a single modality could be competitive. config_014 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, transformer) directly tests the contribution of the image modality while holding the RNA encoder (scgpt) and aggregation (transformer) constant. If RNA alone approaches 0.507, it signals the image branch isn't adding value and I should redirect my remaining 7 experiments toward RNA optimization or image-only variants. If RNA alone is substantially lower, it confirms multimodal is the right direction and I can confidently exploit the multimodal space for the rest of the budget. This is the highest-information experiment at this early stage because it resolves the most consequential design-axis question before committing further budget to fine-grained multimodal ablations.

Evidence: config_005 (multimodal, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) scored 0.507 acc / 0.455 F1, while config_014 (RNA-only, scgpt, transformer) scored 0.514 acc / 0.498 F1. The multimodal model underperformed the RNA-only baseline, suggesting the concat fusion may be introducing noise or misalignment from the image branch. Question: config_010 isolates a single variable—changing fusion from concat to weighted—while keeping scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and multiprofile identical to config_005. This directly tests whether weighted fusion can rescue the multimodal setup or whether the image modality itself is unhelpful. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, a clean single-variable comparison is the most information-efficient next step. If weighted fusion improves over concat, it confirms fusion strategy is the bottleneck and guides subsequent experiments toward better fusion/aggregation combinations. If it still underperforms RNA-only, we can pivot decisively toward RNA-centric or alternative image-encoder configurations, saving budget.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_010 (multimodal, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.520 acc, but rna_only with scgpt+transformer (config_014) is very close at 0.514, suggesting the image modality is contributing only marginally with imagenet_vit_l. This experiment tests whether swapping the image encoder to resnet50 (while keeping scgpt, transformer, weighted fusion) can unlock more value from the image modality. It is the best use of the next slot because it isolates the image encoder as the single variable against the current best, directly addressing the key uncertainty: is the image modality underperforming due to a poor encoder choice, or is it inherently low-value here? The answer will guide whether to invest remaining budget in image-encoder variants or pivot toward RNA-encoder/fusion improvements.

The current best (config_010: scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.520) is only marginally ahead of rna_only (config_014, acc=0.514), suggesting the image modality's contribution is modest and may depend on how the RNA representation interacts with it. All four completed experiments use scgpt as the RNA encoder, so we have no evidence on whether an alternative encoder (scvi_n200, a variational autoencoder with 200-dim latent space) could improve multimodal fusion or reveal a stronger interaction with the image branch. config_045 changes only the RNA encoder from scgpt to scvi_n200 while keeping the otherwise-best settings (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile), making it a clean single-variable test. If scvi_n200 matches or beats scgpt, it opens a broader search space; if it underperforms, it confirms scgpt as the preferred encoder and lets us focus remaining budget on aggregation/fusion refinements around scgpt. With 5 experiments left, resolving this key design axis is the highest-value uncertainty reduction.

Evidence: config_045 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved 0.725 accuracy, a massive jump over all scgpt-based configs (~0.50-0.52), strongly implicating the scvi_n200 RNA encoder as the critical factor. Question: config_007 is a single-variable change from config_045 (fusion: weighted → concat), testing whether the weighted fusion specifically contributes to the high performance or whether the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer backbone is sufficient regardless of fusion. Why: With 4 experiments remaining, I need to confirm which components of the best config are load-bearing. If concat performs comparably, it frees up the fusion dimension and lets me explore other variables (aggregation, image encoder, profile setting) in remaining budget. If it drops, I lock in weighted fusion and focus remaining experiments on other axes. This is the highest-information single experiment to exploit the strong scvi_n200 signal.

Evidence: The top two experiments (config_045 at 0.725, config_007 at 0.721) both use scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer aggregation, with weighted fusion slightly ahead. The RNA encoder (scvi_n200 vs scgpt) is the dominant performance driver (~20-point gap), and imagenet_vit_l outperforms resnet50. However, aggregation method has only been tested as 'transformer' with the best RNA encoder. Question: Does avgpool aggregation with the proven-best components (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion) match or exceed transformer aggregation? This isolates the aggregation variable while holding all other factors at their empirically best settings. Why this is the best use: With only 3 experiments remaining, testing the single unexplored dimension (aggregation) around the current best configuration is the highest-information experiment. If avgpool performs comparably, it confirms the current best is near-optimal; if it underperforms, it confirms transformer is the right choice and we can focus remaining budget on other refinements. config_003 is the most targeted single-variable test from the current best.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted (config_045) is the clear best at 0.725 accuracy, and all other variables (RNA encoder, aggregation, fusion) are well-characterized. The remaining uncertainty is whether the image encoder choice (imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) contributes meaningfully when paired with the strong scvi_n200 RNA encoder. config_035 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) isolates the image encoder variable while holding all other settings at their best-known values. This is the best use of experiment 8 because: (1) it directly tests whether the ~2-3% gap seen between imagenet_vit_l and resnet50 in the scgpt setting persists with scvi_n200, (2) if it performs close to config_045, it broadens the set of viable configurations for the final experiment, and (3) if it performs significantly worse, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is critical and the last experiment should focus on confirming config_045 or a minor perturbation. With only 2 experiments remaining, reducing uncertainty about the image encoder's marginal contribution is the highest-value information gain.

The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion as the top-performing component combination (config_045: 0.725 acc, config_007: 0.721 acc, config_035: 0.713 acc). The only major untested architectural axis with these best encoders is the profile setting: all top performers use multiprofile with transformer aggregation, but singleprofile (which removes the aggregation step entirely) has never been tested with scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l. Config_047 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, singleprofile, weighted) tests whether the simpler single-profile architecture might be competitive or even superior by avoiding potential overfitting in the transformer aggregation. This is the best use of experiment 9 because it explores the last meaningful untested dimension with the proven-best encoders and fusion, and with only 1 experiment remaining after this, it maximizes the chance of either finding a new best or confirming that config_045 is the optimal configuration.

Evidence: The top-4 configs all use scvi_n200 + transformer + multiprofile, with imagenet_vit_l+weighted (config_045, acc=0.725) as the current best. Notably, config_035 (scvi_n200+resnet50+transformer+weighted) achieved a higher F1 (0.6945) than config_045 (0.6847), suggesting resnet50 captures complementary features. Question: config_032 (scvi_n200+resnet50+transformer+concat) is the closest untested point in the high-performing neighborhood, testing whether concat fusion combined with resnet50's complementary feature space could produce a synergy that improves accuracy beyond 0.725. Rationale: With 0 experiments remaining, exploitation in the proven scvi_n200+transformer+multiprofile regime is the only rational strategy. config_032 is the nearest untested configuration to the current best, varying only the two dimensions (image encoder, fusion) that showed the smallest individual gaps, making it the highest-probability candidate to match or exceed the current best.
